walkthrough:
**Identify the organic product**

Great start, let's focus on what is made. The equation shows the only organic product is $2\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CHO}$.

This is propanal: $$\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CHO}$$
It contains the $\text{-CHO}$ group, so it is an aldehyde.

**Test 1 and 2, oxidation of aldehydes**

Aldehydes are very easy to oxidise to carboxylic acids, even with gentle oxidising agents.

Tollens reagent gives a silver mirror with aldehydes, and acidified $\text{MnO}_4^-$ changes from purple to colourless as the aldehyde is oxidised:
$$\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CHO} + [O] \rightarrow \text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{COOH}$$
So both 1 and 2 are positive.

**Test 3, the iodoform test**

Warming with alkaline aqueous iodine is the triiodomethane (iodoform) test. It is positive only for ethanal ($\text{CH}_3\text{CHO}$) and methyl ketones containing the $\text{CH}_3\text{CO}$ group.

Propanal is $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CHO}$. It has a $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2$ group, not a $\text{CH}_3\text{CO}$ group, so no yellow precipitate of $\text{CHI}_3$ forms. So 3 is negative.

**Combine the conclusions**

We have 1 correct, 2 correct, and 3 incorrect.

That corresponds to 1 and 2 only.

options.A: Incorrect. This option claims 1, 2 and 3 are all positive. While 1 and 2 are correct for propanal, 3 is wrong because propanal does not contain the $\text{CH}_3\text{CO}$ group needed for the iodoform test.
options.B: Correct. Propanal is an aldehyde, so it reduces Tollens reagent to give a silver mirror (1) and it decolourises warm acidified $\text{MnO}_4^-$ as it is oxidised to propanoic acid (2). It does not give iodoform with alkaline iodine (3), so 1 and 2 only is right.
options.C: Incorrect. This option claims 2 and 3 only. Test 2 is indeed positive, but test 3 is negative for propanal, and test 1 has been wrongly left out since all aldehydes give a positive Tollens test.
options.D: Incorrect. This option claims 1 only. Test 1 is positive, but test 2 is also positive because acidified manganate(VII) is a strong oxidiser that readily oxidises propanal. Leaving out 2 makes this incomplete.
